/v/history. For life of me I can't figure out why Japan attacked Pearl. Yamamoto knew it was stupid. Why did they do it?

There are a few reasons but a bit of research shows the most prominent reasons were because Japan wanted to keep the States out of their war with China, and they wanted to cripple the American navy. They attacked Pearl Harbor in the hopes of destroying American aircraft carriers, but many of the carriers were already out to sea. That strikes me as odd. I just can't imagine the Japanese having bad intel like that. Surely they would know that one of their main targets weren't actually there? At any rate, they did have some legitimate reasons for attacking Pearl Harbor.

You and I agree, but America had strong reasons and interests to join the European war. Japan and Asia were a sideshow. America was a powerhouse. Even sinking a couple or all of the carriers wouldn't sideline them for long. They (the Americans) had no dog in the Asian fight.

First of all we have to remember that attacking surface warships with aircraft was pretty much a new thing. The only successful torpedo before Pearl Harbor had occurred in 1940 with the British taking out the Italian fleet at Taranto. The Italian fleet anchored at Taranto were 6 battle ships, 9 heavy cruisers, 7 Light cruisers, and 13 destroyers.

The result of the attack was One Italian battleship sunk, 2 heavily damaged, 1 heavy cruiser slightly damaged and two destroyers slightly damaged. Not what you would call a stunning defeat. Even by late 1941 a air attack on a fleet was considered by many in the Japanese naval community to be a risky business.

Up until Pearl Harbor the striking power of a navy rested on its battleships, and in all probability it was the battle ships that japan wanted to neutralize. They (the Japanese) knew that they out numbered American Fleet Carriers by 6 to 5. and light carriers by 6 to 2. They also knew that only three American carriers were present in the Pacific. So the Japanese carrier advantage was 6 to 3.

Now lets look at the carrier forces. The United States in December of 1941 had only 8 Aircraft carriers. Of the 8 the USS Langley, USS Ranger and the USS Wasp were second rate carriers. The Langley was slow (max speed 15 Knots) and carried 36 aircraft. The USS Ranger like the USS Wasp were small ships. They could achieve 30 knots but they both weighed abut 14,000 tons. This light weight meant that the lack of armor and redundant systems would be a serious deficiency in actual combat. This lack of Armor and redundant systems would lead to sinking of the Wasp on her frist combat patrol. When pearl harbor occurred all three of the light weight carriers were in the Atlantic.

That just left the US with 5 fleet carriers. USS Lexington and USS Saratoga, where were built on converted battle cruiser hulls. This conversion while giving the ships the ability to take a lot of punishment also made the launching, recovery and handling of aircraft on deck a long drawn out affair. Both the Lexington and Saratoga were stationed in the pacific and on the way to deliver aircraft to wake Island when Pearl harbor occurred. The final Pacific Fleet Carrier was the USS Enterprise and it was on it's way back to Pearl Harbor when the attack occurred. In Fact the Enterprise docked at Pearl Harbor late in the day of December 7th. There is some speculation that if the Japanese had be doing any recon they might have found the Enterprise and added her to the bag list.

So to make a long story short the Japanese knew that the US Navy only had three fleet carriers in the pacific at the time of pearl harbor. For the pearl harbor raid the Japanese sent all six of their fleet carriers. (The remaining 6 light carriers were used to support attacks on Malaya, the Philippians, and the Dutch east Indies.

The Attack was necessary to keep the United States from intervening in the planned military operations to seize the oil and mineral deposits of South East Asia that Japan needed to continue the war effort in China.

A little side note. At Pearl Harbor the Untied States had 4 Battleships sunk and 4 heavily damaged. That still left the Navy with 9 Battle ships. 15 heavy Cruisers, 19 light Cruisers And 360 Destroyers. Of the 4 battleships damaged at Pearl Harbor 3 were fully repaired and combat ready by Feb of 1942.

So as of Feb of 1942 the American navy was superior in ship numbers to the Japanese navy. But unlike the Japanese navy the US Navy was forced to fight a two front war which caused a considerable number of U.S. Navy ships to be deployed in the Atlantic.
